sanskrit: tataḥ sahasraṃ viprāṇāṃ caturvedavidāṃ tathā gavāṃ sahasreṇaikaikaṃ vācayām āsa mādhavaḥ
english: Then Mādhava caused a thousand brāhmaṇas, each versed in the four Vedas, to pronounce their benedictions, presenting to each one a thousand cows.

sanskrit: maṅgalālambhanaṃ kṛtvā ātmānam avalokya ca ādarśe vimale kṛṣṇas tataḥ sātyakim abravīt
english: Having performed the rites of auspicious touch and beheld himself in a spotless mirror, Kṛṣṇa then spoke to Sātyaki.

sanskrit: gaccha śaineya jānīhi gatvā rājaniveśanam api sajjo mahātejā bhīṣmaṃ draṣṭuṃ yuthiṣṭhiraḥ
english: "Go, scion of Śini, go to the king's dwelling and learn whether the mighty-splendored Yudhiṣṭhira is ready to go and behold Bhīṣma."

sanskrit: tataḥ kṛṣṇasya vacanāt sātyakis tvarito yayau upagamya ca rājānaṃ yudhiṣṭhiram uvāca ha
english: Then at Kṛṣṇa's word Sātyaki went swiftly, and approaching King Yudhiṣṭhira he spoke.

sanskrit: yukto rathavaro rājan vāsudevasya dhīmataḥ samīpam āpageyasya prayāsyati janārdanaḥ
english: "The fine chariot of wise Vāsudeva is yoked, O king; Janārdana will set out for the presence of the son of the river-goddess."

sanskrit: bhavatpratīkṣaḥ kṛṣṇo 'sau dharmarāja mahādyute yad atrānantaraṃ kṛtyaṃ tad bhavān kartum arhati
english: "That Kṛṣṇa awaits you, O Dharmarāja of great splendor; whatever should next be done in this matter, that you ought to do."

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca yujyatāṃ me rathavaraḥ phalgunāpratimadyute na sainikaiś ca yātavyaṃ yāsyāmo vayam eva hi
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: "Let my fine chariot be yoked, O Phalguna of incomparable splendor; we must not go with soldiers — we ourselves alone shall go."

sanskrit: na ca pīḍayitavyo me bhīṣmo dharmabhṛtāṃ varaḥ ataḥ puraḥsarāś cāpi nivartantu dhanaṃjaya
english: "And Bhīṣma, the foremost of the upholders of dharma, must not be troubled by me; therefore let even the forerunners turn back, O Dhanaṃjaya."

sanskrit: adyaprabhṛti gāṅgeyaḥ paraṃ guhyaṃ pravakṣyati tato necchāmi kaunteya pṛthagjanasamāgamam
english: "From this day onward the son of Gaṅgā will declare the highest mystery; therefore, O son of Kuntī, I do not wish for any gathering of common folk."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tad vākyam ākarṇya tathā kuntīputro dhanaṃjayaḥ yuktaṃ rathavaraṃ tasmā ācacakṣe nararṣabha
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having heard that speech, Dhanaṃjaya the son of Kuntī announced to him, O bull among men, that the fine chariot was yoked.

sanskrit: tato yudhiṣṭhiro rājā yamau bhīmārjunāv api bhūtānīva samastāni yayuḥ kṛṣṇaniveśanam
english: Then King Yudhiṣṭhira, with the twins and with Bhīma and Arjuna, set out for Kṛṣṇa's dwelling — like all created beings come together.

sanskrit: āgacchatsv atha kṛṣṇo 'pi pāṇḍaveṣu mahātmasu śaineyasahito dhīmān ratham evānvapadyata
english: As those great-souled Pāṇḍavas were approaching, the wise Kṛṣṇa too, together with the scion of Śini, mounted his chariot.

sanskrit: rathasthāḥ saṃvidaṃ kṛtvā sukhāṃ pṛṣṭvā ca śarvarīm meghaghoṣai rathavaraiḥ prayayus te mahārathāḥ
english: Standing in their chariots, having greeted one another and inquired after a comfortable night, those great chariot-warriors set out in fine chariots that rumbled like thunderclouds.

sanskrit: meghapuṣpaṃ balāhaṃ ca sainyaṃ sugrīvam eva ca dārukaś codayām āsa vāsudevasya vājinaḥ
english: Dāruka urged on Vāsudeva's horses — Meghapuṣpa and Balāhaka, Sainya and Sugrīva.

sanskrit: te hayā vāsudevasya dārukeṇa pracoditāḥ gāṃ khurāgrais tathā rājaṃl likhantaḥ prayayus tadā
english: Those horses of Vāsudeva, driven on by Dāruka, then sped forward, O king, scoring the earth with the tips of their hooves.

sanskrit: te grasanta ivākāśaṃ vegavanto mahābalāḥ kṣetraṃ dharmasya kṛtsnasya kurukṣetram avātaran
english: Swift and mighty, as though devouring the sky, they descended upon Kurukṣetra, the field of dharma entire.

sanskrit: tato yayur yatra bhīṣmaḥ śaratalpagataḥ prabhuḥ āste brahmarṣibhiḥ sārdhaṃ brahmā devagaṇair yathā
english: Then they went to where the lord Bhīṣma lay upon his bed of arrows, surrounded by brahmin-seers as Brahmā is by the hosts of gods.

sanskrit: tato 'vatīrya govindo rathāt sa ca yudhiṣṭhiraḥ bhīmo gāṇḍīvadhanvā ca yamau sātyakir eva ca ṛṣīn abhyarcayām āsuḥ karān udyamya dakṣiṇān
english: Then Govinda alighted from the chariot, and so did Yudhiṣṭhira, Bhīma, the wielder of the Gāṇḍīva, the twins, and Sātyaki; raising their right hands, they paid honor to the seers.

sanskrit: sa taiḥ parivṛto rājā nakṣatrair iva candramāḥ abhyājagāma gāṅgeyaṃ brahmāṇam iva vāsavaḥ
english: Encircled by them like the moon by the constellations, the king approached the son of Gaṅgā as Vāsava approaches Brahmā.

sanskrit: śaratalpe śayānaṃ tam ādityaṃ patitaṃ yathā dadarśa sa mahābāhur bhayād āgatasādhvasaḥ
english: That mighty-armed one, gripped by dread out of fear, gazed upon him lying on his bed of arrows like the fallen sun.

sanskrit: janamejaya uvāca dharmātmani mahāsattve satyasaṃdhe jitātmani devavrate mahābhāge śaratalpagate 'cyute
english: Janamejaya said: "When the righteous one of great spirit, true to his word, master of himself, vowed to the gods, the blessed and unfaltering Bhīṣma lay upon his bed of arrows —

sanskrit: śayāne vīraśayane bhīṣme śaṃtanunandane gāṅgeye puruṣavyāghre pāṇḍavaiḥ paryupasthite
english: "when Bhīṣma, the delight of Śaṃtanu, the son of Gaṅgā, that tiger among men, lay upon the hero's couch, attended on every side by the Pāṇḍavas —

sanskrit: kāḥ kathāḥ samavartanta tasmin vīrasamāgame hateṣu sarvasainyeṣu tan me śaṃsa mahāmune
english: "what discourses arose at that gathering of heroes, when all the armies had been slain? Relate that to me, O great sage."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca śaratalpagate bhīṣme kauravāṇāṃ dhuraṃdhare ājagmur ṛṣayaḥ siddhā nāradapramukhā nṛpa
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: When Bhīṣma, the burden-bearer of the Kurus, lay upon his bed of arrows, the perfected seers, with Nārada at their head, came near, O king.

sanskrit: hataśiṣṭāś ca rājāno yudhiṣṭhirapurogamāḥ dhṛtarāṣṭraś ca kṛṣṇaś ca bhīmārjunayamās tathā
english: And the kings who had survived the slaughter, with Yudhiṣṭhira at their head, and Dhṛtarāṣṭra and Kṛṣṇa, and Bhīma, Arjuna, and the twins as well.

sanskrit: te 'bhigamya mahātmāno bharatānāṃ pitāmaham anvaśocanta gāṅgeyam ādityaṃ patitaṃ yathā
english: Those great-souled ones, drawing near to the grandsire of the Bhāratas, the son of Gaṅgā, grieved over him as over the fallen sun.

sanskrit: muhūrtam iva ca dhyātvā nārado devadarśanaḥ uvāca pāṇḍavān sarvān hataśiṣṭāṃś ca pārthivān
english: And having reflected for a moment, Nārada, whose vision is godlike, spoke to all the Pāṇḍavas and to the surviving princes.

sanskrit: prāptakālaṃ ca ācakṣe bhīṣmo 'yam anuyujyatām astam eti hi gāṅgeyo bhānumān iva bhārata
english: He declared that the time had come: "Let this Bhīṣma be questioned, for the son of Gaṅgā is setting like the radiant sun, O descendant of Bharata."

sanskrit: ayaṃ prāṇān utsisṛkṣus taṃ sarve 'bhyetya pṛcchata kṛtsnān hi vividhān dharmāṃś cāturvarṇyasya vetty ayam
english: "He is about to surrender his life-breaths; draw near to him, all of you, and ask, for he knows the whole and manifold duties of the four orders."

sanskrit: eṣa vṛddhaḥ purā lokān saṃprāpnoti tanutyajām taṃ śīghram anuyuñjadhvaṃ saṃśayān manasi sthitān
english: "This aged one will soon attain the worlds of those who cast off the body; question him quickly upon the doubts that abide in your minds."

sanskrit: evam uktā nāradena bhīṣmam īyur narādhipāḥ praṣṭuṃ cāśaknuvantas te vīkṣāṃ cakruḥ parasparam
english: Thus addressed by Nārada, the rulers of men went up to Bhīṣma; but, unable to question him, they looked upon one another.

sanskrit: athovāca hṛṣīkeśaṃ pāṇḍuputro yudhiṣṭhiraḥ nānyas tvad devakīputra śaktaḥ praṣṭuṃ pitāmaham
english: Then Yudhiṣṭhira, the son of Pāṇḍu, said to Hṛṣīkeśa: "None other than you, O son of Devakī, is able to question the grandsire."

sanskrit: pravyāhāraya durdharṣa tvam agre madhusūdana tvaṃ hi nas tāta sarveṣāṃ sarvadharmavid uttamaḥ
english: "Do you, O invincible slayer of Madhu, draw him first into speech; for you, dear one, are the supreme knower of all dharma among us all."

sanskrit: evam uktaḥ pāṇḍavena bhagavān keśavas tadā abhigamya durādharṣaṃ pravyāhārayad acyutaḥ
english: Thus addressed by the Pāṇḍava, the blessed and unfaltering Keśava then approached the unassailable one and drew him into speech.

sanskrit: vāsudeva uvāca kaccit sukhena rajanī vyuṣṭā te rājasattama vispaṣṭalakṣaṇā buddhiḥ kaccic copasthitā tava
english: Vāsudeva said: "Has the night passed in comfort for you, O best of kings? Has your understanding, with its faculties unclouded, returned to you?"

sanskrit: kaccij jñānāni sarvāṇi pratibhānti ca te 'nagha na glāyate ca hṛdayaṃ na ca te vyākulaṃ manaḥ
english: "Do all branches of knowledge shine clear within you, O sinless one? Is your heart not faint, and is your mind not distressed?"

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca dāho mohaḥ śramaś caiva klamo glānis tathā rujā tava prasādād govinda sadyo vyapagatānagha
english: Bhīṣma said: "Burning and bewilderment, weariness and exhaustion, faintness and pain — all at once, by your grace, O sinless Govinda, have departed."

sanskrit: yac ca bhūtaṃ bhaviṣyac ca bhavac ca paramadyute tat sarvam anupaśyāmi pāṇau phalam ivāhitam
english: "What has been and what shall be and what now is, O one of supreme splendor — all that I behold, like a fruit set in the palm of my hand."

sanskrit: vedoktāś caiva ye dharmā vedāntanihitāś ca ye tān sarvān saṃprapaśyāmi varadānāt tavācyuta
english: "The duties declared in the Vedas, and those laid down in the Vedānta — all of them I clearly perceive through the boon you have granted, O unfaltering one."

sanskrit: śiṣṭaiś ca dharmo yaḥ proktaḥ sa ca me hṛdi vartate deśajātikulānāṃ ca dharmajño 'smi janārdana
english: "The dharma declared by the virtuous, that too abides in my heart; and I am a knower of the duties of countries, castes, and families, O Janārdana."

sanskrit: caturṣv āśramadharmeṣu yo 'rthaḥ sa ca hṛdi sthitaḥ rājadharmāṃś ca sakalān avagacchāmi keśava
english: "The meaning that lies in the duties of the four stations of life, that too is fixed in my heart; and I comprehend the duties of kings in their entirety, O Keśava."

sanskrit: yatra yatra ca vaktavyaṃ tad vakṣyāmi janārdana tava prasādād dhi śubhā mano me buddhir āviśat
english: "And wherever something must be said, that I shall say, O Janārdana; for by your grace an auspicious understanding has entered my mind."

sanskrit: yuveva cāsmi saṃvṛttas tvadanudhyānabṛṃhitaḥ vaktuṃ śreyaḥ samartho 'smi tvatprasādāj janārdana
english: "I have become as it were a youth again, fortified by meditation upon you; I am able to speak of what is best, by your grace, O Janārdana."

sanskrit: svayaṃ kimarthaṃ tu bhavāñ śreyo na prāha pāṇḍavam kiṃ te vivakṣitaṃ cātra tad āśu vada mādhava
english: "But why do you yourself not declare what is best to the Pāṇḍava? What is it you wish to say in this matter? Tell it quickly, O Mādhava."

sanskrit: vāsudeva uvāca yaśasaḥ śreyasaś caiva mūlaṃ māṃ viddhi kaurava mattaḥ sarve 'bhinirvṛttā bhāvāḥ sadasadātmakāḥ
english: Vāsudeva said: "Know me to be the root of glory and of the good, O Kaurava; from me have all states of being arisen, whose nature is the existent and the non-existent."

sanskrit: śītāṃśuś candra ity ukte ko loke vismayiṣyati tathaiva yaśasā pūrṇe mayi ko vismayiṣyati
english: "When the cool-rayed one is called the moon, who in the world would marvel? Just so, when I am full of glory, who would marvel?"

sanskrit: ādheyaṃ tu mayā bhūyo yaśas tava mahādyute tato me vipulā buddhis tvayi bhīṣma samāhitā
english: "But further glory is to be conferred upon you by me, O one of great splendor; therefore, Bhīṣma, my abundant resolve has been set upon you."

sanskrit: yāvad dhi pṛthivīpāla pṛthivī sthāsyate dhruvā tāvat tavākṣayā kīrtir lokān anu cariṣyati
english: "For as long as the earth shall stand firm, O protector of the earth, so long shall your undying fame range throughout the worlds."

sanskrit: yac ca tvaṃ vakṣyase bhīṣma pāṇḍavāyānupṛcchate vedapravādā iva te sthāsyanti vasudhātale
english: "And whatever you shall declare, Bhīṣma, to the Pāṇḍava who questions you, shall endure upon the face of the earth like the pronouncements of the Vedas."

sanskrit: yaś caitena pramāṇena yokṣyaty ātmānam ātmanā sa phalaṃ sarvapuṇyānāṃ pretya cānubhaviṣyati
english: "And whoever shall yoke himself to himself by this authoritative measure shall, after death, enjoy the fruit of all meritorious deeds."

sanskrit: etasmāt kāraṇād bhīṣma matir divyā mayā hi te dattā yaśo vipratheta kathaṃ bhūyas taveti ha
english: "For this reason, Bhīṣma, a divine understanding has been bestowed upon you by me — that your glory might spread the more abroad."

sanskrit: yāvad dhi prathate loke puruṣasya yaśo bhuvi tāvat tasyākṣayaṃ sthānaṃ bhavatīti viniścitam
english: "For as long as a man's fame spreads in the world upon the earth, so long, it is determined, does his imperishable station endure."

sanskrit: rājāno hataśiṣṭās tvāṃ rājann abhita āsate dharmān anuyuyukṣantas tebhyaḥ prabrūhi bhārata
english: "The kings who survived the slaughter sit about you, O king, wishing to inquire into the duties of dharma; expound them to these, O descendant of Bharata."

sanskrit: bhavān hi vayasā vṛddhaḥ śrutācārasamanvitaḥ kuśalo rājadharmāṇāṃ pūrveṣām aparāś ca ye
english: "For you are advanced in years, endowed with learning and good conduct, and skilled in the duties of kings, both those of old and those that came after."

sanskrit: janmaprabhṛti te kaś cid vṛjinaṃ na dadarśa ha jñātāram anudharmāṇāṃ tvāṃ viduḥ sarvapārthivāḥ
english: "From your birth onward no one has ever seen a crookedness in you; all the princes know you as one who understands the subtleties of dharma."

sanskrit: tebhyaḥ piteva putrebhyo rājan brūhi paraṃ nayam ṛṣayaś ca hi devāś ca tvayā nityam upāsitāḥ
english: "To them, O king, as a father to his sons, declare the highest polity; for the seers and the gods have ever been honored by you."

sanskrit: tasmād vaktavyam eveha tvayā paśyāmy aśeṣataḥ dharmāñ śuśrūṣamāṇebhyaḥ pṛṣṭena ca satā punaḥ
english: "Therefore it must indeed be spoken by you here, as I see it without remainder — the duties of dharma, to those who wish to learn, and again to one who, being good, is asked."

sanskrit: vaktavyaṃ viduṣā ceti dharmam āhur manīṣiṇaḥ apratibruvataḥ kaṣṭo doṣo hi bhavati prabho
english: "And it should be spoken by the learned — so the wise declare to be dharma; for a grievous fault befalls one who does not answer, O lord."

sanskrit: tasmāt putraiś ca pautraiś ca dharmān pṛṣṭaḥ sanātanān vidvāñ jijñāsamānais tvaṃ prabrūhi bharatarṣabha
english: "Therefore, being questioned about the eternal duties of dharma by sons and grandsons who seek to know, do you, learned one, expound them, O bull of the Bhāratas."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca athābravīn mahātejā vākyaṃ kauravanandanaḥ hanta dharmān pravakṣyāmi dṛḍhe vāṅmanasī mama tava prasādād govinda bhūtātmā hy asi śāśvataḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then the mighty-splendored delight of the Kurus spoke these words: "So be it — I shall declare the duties of dharma; firm now are my speech and my mind by your grace, O Govinda, for you are the eternal self of all beings."

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhiras tu māṃ rājā dharmān samanupṛcchatu evaṃ prīto bhaviṣyāmi dharmān vakṣyāmi cānagha
english: "But let King Yudhiṣṭhira question me about the duties of dharma; thus shall I be pleased, and I shall declare those duties, O sinless one."

sanskrit: yasmin rājarṣabhe jāte dharmātmani mahātmani ahṛṣyann ṛṣayaḥ sarve sa māṃ pṛcchatu pāṇḍavaḥ
english: "At whose birth — that bull among kings, righteous and great-souled — all the seers rejoiced: let that Pāṇḍava question me."

sanskrit: sarveṣāṃ dīptayaśasāṃ kurūṇāṃ dharmacāriṇām yasya nāsti samaḥ kaś cit sa māṃ pṛcchatu pāṇḍavaḥ
english: "He to whom there is no equal among all the Kurus of blazing fame who walk in dharma: let that Pāṇḍava question me."

sanskrit: dhṛtir damo brahmacaryaṃ kṣamā dharmaś ca nityadā yasminn ojaś ca tejaś ca sa māṃ pṛcchatu pāṇḍavaḥ
english: "He in whom dwell ever firmness, self-restraint, chastity, forbearance, and dharma, and vigor and splendor: let that Pāṇḍava question me."

sanskrit: satyaṃ dānaṃ tapaḥ śaucaṃ śāntir dākṣyam asaṃbhramaḥ yasminn etāni sarvāṇi sa māṃ pṛcchatu pāṇḍavaḥ
english: "He in whom are all these — truth, charity, austerity, purity, tranquility, skill, and composure: let that Pāṇḍava question me."

sanskrit: yo na kāmān na saṃrambhān na bhayān nārthakāraṇāt kuryād adharmaṃ dharmātmā sa māṃ pṛcchatu pāṇḍavaḥ
english: "He, righteous of soul, who would not, from desire nor anger, nor fear nor for the sake of gain, commit unrighteousness: let that Pāṇḍava question me."

sanskrit: saṃbandhino 'tithīn bhṛtyān saṃśritopāśritāṃś ca yaḥ saṃmānayati satkṛtya sa māṃ pṛcchatu pāṇḍavaḥ
english: "He who honors with hospitality his kinsmen, guests, and servants, and those who seek shelter and dependence with him: let that Pāṇḍava question me."

sanskrit: satyanityaḥ kṣamānityo jñānanityo 'tithipriyaḥ yo dadāti satāṃ nityaṃ sa māṃ pṛcchatu pāṇḍavaḥ
english: "He who is ever true, ever forbearing, ever devoted to knowledge, fond of guests, and who gives always to the virtuous: let that Pāṇḍava question me."

sanskrit: ijyādhyayananityaś ca dharme ca nirataḥ sadā śāntaḥ śrutarahasyaś ca sa māṃ pṛcchatu pāṇḍavaḥ
english: "He who is ever devoted to sacrifice and study, and always intent upon dharma, tranquil, and versed in the secret of sacred lore: let that Pāṇḍava question me."

sanskrit: vāsudeva uvāca lajjayā parayopeto dharmātmā sa yudhiṣṭhiraḥ abhiśāpabhayād bhīto bhavantaṃ nopasarpati
english: Vāsudeva said: "Possessed of utmost modesty, that righteous Yudhiṣṭhira, terrified by the fear of your curse, does not approach you."

sanskrit: lokasya kadanaṃ kṛtvā lokanātho viśāṃ pate abhiśāpabhayād bhīto bhavantaṃ nopasarpati
english: "Having wrought the destruction of the world, this lord of the world, O ruler of peoples, terrified by the fear of your curse, does not approach you."

sanskrit: pūjyān mānyāṃś ca bhaktāṃś ca gurūn saṃbandhibāndhavān arghyārhān iṣubhir hatvā bhavantaṃ nopasarpati
english: "Having slain with his arrows those worthy of worship and honor — the devoted, the elders, kinsmen, and friends, all deserving the guest-offering — he does not approach you."

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca brāhmaṇānāṃ yathā dharmo dānam adhyayanaṃ tapaḥ kṣatriyāṇāṃ tathā kṛṣṇa samare dehapātanam
english: Bhīṣma said: "As the dharma of brāhmaṇas is charity, study, and austerity, so for kṣatriyas, O Kṛṣṇa, it is the casting down of the body in battle."

sanskrit: pitṝn pitāmahān putrān gurūn saṃbandhibāndhavān mithyāpravṛttān yaḥ saṃkhye nihanyād dharma eva saḥ
english: "He who slays in battle fathers, grandfathers, sons, elders, kinsmen, and friends who have set out in a wrongful cause — that is dharma indeed."

sanskrit: samayatyāgino lubdhān gurūn api ca keśava nihanti samare pāpān kṣatriyo yaḥ sa dharmavit
english: "The kṣatriya who slays in battle those wicked men who have broken their compact and are greedy — even elders, O Keśava — he is a knower of dharma."

sanskrit: āhūtena raṇe nityaṃ yoddhavyaṃ kṣatrabandhunā dharmyaṃ svargyaṃ ca lokyaṃ ca yuddhaṃ hi manur abravīt
english: "When challenged in battle, the kinsman of the warrior-caste must always fight; for war is in accord with dharma, conducive to heaven and to the worlds — so Manu declared."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca evam uktas tu bhīṣmeṇa dharmarājo yudhiṣṭhiraḥ vinītavad upāgamya tasthau saṃdarśane 'grataḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Thus addressed by Bhīṣma, the Dharmarāja Yudhiṣṭhira drew near humbly and stood before him in his sight.

sanskrit: athāsya pādau jagrāha bhīṣmaś cābhinananda tam mūrdhni cainam upāghrāya niṣīdety abravīt tadā
english: Then he clasped his feet, and Bhīṣma welcomed him, and kissing him upon the head, said to him then: "Be seated."

sanskrit: tam uvācātha gāṅgeya ṛṣabhaḥ sarvadhanvinām pṛccha māṃ tāta visrabdhaṃ mā bhais tvaṃ kurusattama
english: Then the son of Gaṅgā, the bull among all bowmen, said to him: "Question me freely, dear son; have no fear, O best of the Kurus."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca praṇipatya hṛṣīkeśam abhivādya pitāmaham anumānya gurūn sarvān paryapṛcchad yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having bowed down to Hṛṣīkeśa and saluted the grandsire, and having sought the leave of all his elders, Yudhiṣṭhira began to question him.
